items.en: How the Eight Forms of Detachment Lead Toward the Path
parent: The Eight Forms of Detachment: Naming, Stages, and Method
八背捨 · 釋名 · 次位 · 觀法不同

zh: 第五、分別趣道之相。行者修八背捨入道，有三種不同：一者、先用背捨破遮道法，後則具足修習勝處，乃至超越三昧，事、理二觀具足，方發真無漏，證三乘道。二者、若修八背捨時，是人厭離生死，欲速得解脫，是時遍修緣諦真觀等，即於八背捨中發真無漏，證三乘道，亦名具足八解脫也。當知此人未必具下五種法門。
en: Fifth, distinguishing the mark of how detachment leads toward the path. The practitioner cultivating the eight forms of detachment enters the path in three differing ways.

First, one first uses detachment to break through the dharmas obstructing the path, and only afterward becomes complete in cultivating the stations of mastery, and, further still, the samādhi of transcendence — the two contemplations of concrete phenomena and of principle both complete, only then does true undefilement arise, and the path of the three vehicles is realized.

Second, should one, while cultivating the eight forms of detachment, already be so wearied by and detached from birth-and-death that one wishes to swiftly obtain liberation, at that time one broadly cultivates the true contemplation taking the truths as object and the rest, and true undefilement thereby arises within the eight forms of detachment themselves, the path of the three vehicles realized, also named being complete with the eight liberations. One should know that this person need not necessarily be complete with the remaining five dharma-gates below.

zh: 問曰：若爾，此人未得九次第定，云何已得受八解脫之名？答曰：是義應作四句分別：一者自有九次第定非解脫，自有是解脫非次第定，自有次第定亦是解脫，自有非次第定非解脫，而是八背捨。三者、若人厭離生死心重，但證初背捨時，即深觀四諦真定之理，無漏若發，便於此地入金剛三昧，證三乘道，當知是人亦復未必具上七種背捨。菩薩摩訶薩心如虛空，無所取捨，以方便力，善修背捨，具足成就一切佛法，度脫眾生。當知背捨即是菩薩摩訶衍。
en: Question: if this is so, this person has not yet obtained the nine sequential concentrations — how, then, does he already receive the name of being complete with the eight liberations? Answer: this sense should be distinguished through four propositions: first, there is the case of one who possesses the nine sequential concentrations but not liberation; second, there is the case of one who possesses liberation but not the sequential concentrations; third, there is the case of one who possesses both the sequential concentrations and liberation together; and fourth, there is the case of one who possesses neither the sequential concentrations nor liberation, and yet still possesses the eight forms of detachment.

Third, should a person's mind be so heavy with weariness toward and detachment from birth-and-death that, upon realizing only the first detachment, he already deeply contemplates the truth of the Four Noble Truths' own real concentration, and, should the undefiled arise, thereupon enters the vajra samādhi at this very stage and realizes the path of the three vehicles — one should know that this person, too, need not necessarily be complete with the seven remaining forms of detachment above.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva, the mind like empty space, grasping and relinquishing nothing at all, through the power of skillful means, skillfully cultivates detachment, becoming complete with the accomplishment of the whole Buddhadharma, and delivers sentient beings across. One should know, then, that detachment is itself precisely the bodhisattva's own Mahāyāna.

The four-proposition breakdown answering "how can someone be called liberated without the nine sequential concentrations?" is a clean piece of logical housekeeping — the treatise is careful to specify that the full sequence — detachment followed by the five further dharma-gates below it — describes a typical, not a mandatory, route, and that swift, partial paths to realization (even from the very first detachment alone) are explicitly acknowledged as valid. This closes the eight forms of detachment exactly as fascicle 9 closed the nine contemplations, eight recollections, and ten perceptions before it: with the same formula naming the practice "the bodhisattva's own Mahāyāna."

items.en: The Eight Stations of Mastery: Naming, Stages, and Mastering a Small Object
items.zh: 八勝處 · 釋名 · 階位 · 勝知見一二

zh: 次釋八勝處法門。八勝處者：一、內有色相，外觀色少，若好若醜，是名勝知勝見一勝處也；二、內有色相，外觀色多，若好若醜，是名勝知見二勝處也；三、內無色相，外觀色少，若好若醜，是名勝知見三勝處也；四、內無色相，外觀色多，若好若醜，是名勝知見四勝處也；五、青勝處；六、黃勝處；七、赤勝處；八、白勝處。若依《纓絡經》，用四大為四勝處。今明勝處，即為四意：一者、釋名；二、明階位；三、辯修證之相；四、明趣道。
en: Next, explaining the dharma-gate of the eight stations of mastery. The eight stations of mastery are: first, form within, contemplating little form without, whether good or ill — this is named the first station of mastery, of superior knowledge and vision; second, form within, contemplating much form without, whether good or ill — this is named the second station of mastery, of superior knowledge and vision; third, no form within, contemplating little form without, whether good or ill — this is named the third station of mastery, of superior knowledge and vision; fourth, no form within, contemplating much form without, whether good or ill — this is named the fourth station of mastery, of superior knowledge and vision; fifth, the station of mastery of blue-green; sixth, the station of mastery of yellow; seventh, the station of mastery of red; eighth, the station of mastery of white. Following the Sūtra of the Original Acts That Adorn a Bodhisattva, the four elements are taken as the four stations of mastery.

Explaining the stations of mastery now has four senses: first, explaining the name; second, clarifying their stages; third, distinguishing the mark of their cultivation and realization; fourth, clarifying how they lead toward the path.

zh: 第一、釋名。此八法通明勝處者，則有二義：一者、若淨若不淨五欲，得此觀時，隨意能破，故名勝處；二者、善調觀心，譬如乘馬擊賊，非但破前陣，亦能善制其馬，故名勝處。此則有異背捨。經亦說為八除入。若因勝處斷煩惱盡，則知虛妄陰入皆滅，爾時勝處變名八除入也。第二、明次位者，今但依《摩訶衍》中說，初二勝處，位在初禪；次第三、第四勝處，位在二禪；後四勝處，位在四禪。所以三禪不立勝處者，以樂多心鈍故。前二禪離欲界近，欲界煩惱難破，雖位居二禪，猶觀不淨，破下地結。四禪既是色中之極，故色勝位極於此。四空既無色故，亦以破地煩惱薄故，故不立勝處。
en: First, explaining the name: as for why these eight dharmas are, in general, called stations of mastery — this has two senses. First, whether the five desires be pure or impure, once one obtains this contemplation, one is thereby able to break through them at will — hence this is named a station of mastery. Second, one skillfully regulates the contemplating mind — like a rider on horseback striking at a bandit, not only breaking through the enemy's own line, but also skillfully mastering the horse itself — hence this, too, is named a station of mastery. This, then, differs from detachment. The sutras also speak of this as the eight bases of removal. Should one, through the stations of mastery, sever affliction entirely, one thereby knows that the illusory aggregates and sense-bases are all extinguished — at that time, the stations of mastery are renamed the eight bases of removal.

Second, clarifying their stages: here, following only what is explained in the Mahāyāna treatise, the first two stations of mastery are placed at the first dhyāna; the third and fourth stations of mastery, next, are placed at the second dhyāna; and the last four stations of mastery are placed at the fourth dhyāna. As for why no station of mastery is established at the third dhyāna: because happiness there is too abundant and the mind too dull. The first two dhyānas lie close to the desire realm, whose afflictions are difficult to break through — hence, though placed within the second dhyāna, one still contemplates impurity there, breaking through the lower stage's own fetters. The fourth dhyāna, being the very utmost of the form realm, is thus where form's own mastery reaches its own limit. The four formless states, already lacking form entirely, and their own afflictions already thin, have, for this reason, no station of mastery established within them either.

zh: 第三、明修證。所以言「內有色相，外觀色少」者，緣少故名少。觀道未增故，觀少因緣，觀多畏難攝故。譬如鹿遊未調，則不中遠放。云何名觀少？行者自觀見己身不淨，亦觀所愛之人不淨、脹爛、白骨，心甚厭惡，如初背捨中說。「若好若醜」者，觀外諸色，善業果報故名好，惡業報故名醜。復次，行者從師所受觀法，觀外緣種種不淨，是名醜色。行者或時憶念，妄生淨想，觀淨色，是好色。復次，行者自身中繫心一處，觀欲界中色有二種：一者、能生婬欲；二者、能生瞋恚。能生婬欲是淨色，名為好；能生瞋恚者是不淨色，故名醜。
en: Third, clarifying cultivation and realization: as for why it is said "form within, contemplating little form without" — since the object taken is small, this is named little. Because the contemplative path has not yet increased in strength, one contemplates a small object as the condition; contemplating a large object is feared too difficult to master. It is like a deer not yet tamed, which should not, then, be let loose to roam too far.

What is meant by "contemplating little"? The practitioner contemplates his own body's own impurity, and also contemplates the impurity, swelling, decay, and white bones of the person he loves, the mind deeply wearied and revolted — as already explained within the first detachment. As for "whether good or ill": contemplating external forms in general, that born of wholesome karmic fruit is named good, and that born of unwholesome karmic retribution is named ill. Furthermore, the practitioner, receiving this contemplative method from a teacher, contemplates every kind of external impurity as its object — this is named ill form. Should the practitioner, at times, recollect and falsely give rise to a perception of purity, and contemplate a pure form — this is good form. Furthermore, the practitioner, fixing the mind upon a single point within his own body, contemplates that form within the desire realm is of two kinds: first, that able to give rise to lustful desire; second, that able to give rise to anger and hatred. That able to give rise to lustful desire is pure form, named good; that able to give rise to anger and hatred is impure form, hence named ill.

zh: 「勝知勝見」者，觀心淳熟，於好色中，心不貪愛，於醜色中，心不瞋恚，但觀色四大因緣和合而生，如水沫不堅固，智慧深達假實之相。行者住是不淨門中，婬欲、瞋恚諸結使來能不隨，故名勝處。勝是不淨中淨，顛倒諸煩惱故。復次，好醜者，不淨觀有二種：一者、見自身、他身三十六物臭穢不淨，是名醜；二者、除內外皮肉五臟，但觀白骨如珂如雪，乃至流光照耀，是名為好。行者見不淨時，即知虛假，心不畏沒；見淨色時，知從緣生，心不愛染，是名勝知勝見。復次，行者於少緣中隨意觀色，轉變自在，亦能善制觀心，故名勝處。
en: As for "superior knowledge, superior vision": the contemplating mind having grown mature, within good form the mind no longer craves or loves it, and within ill form the mind no longer grows angry or hateful toward it, but simply contemplates that form arises from the union of the four elements' own causes and conditions, like foam upon water, without any solidity at all, wisdom penetrating deeply into the mark of the provisional and the real. The practitioner, abiding within this very gate of impurity, is no longer swept along by the fetters of lustful desire and anger and hatred as they arise — hence this is named a station of mastery. "Mastery" is the purity found within impurity, since it overturns every affliction.

Furthermore, "good" and "ill" themselves admit of two kinds of contemplation of impurity: first, seeing one's own body and another's body's own thirty-six substances, stinking and filthy, impure — this is named ill; second, removing the internal and external skin, flesh, and five organs, contemplating only the white bone, like agate, like snow, and, further still, its flowing light radiating forth — this is named good. The practitioner, seeing impurity, thereby knows it to be empty and illusory, the mind no longer fearful and overwhelmed by it; seeing pure form, knows it to arise from conditions, the mind no longer stained by love for it — this is named superior knowledge, superior vision. Furthermore, the practitioner, within a small object, contemplating form at will, transforming it freely, is also thereby able to skillfully master the contemplating mind itself — hence this is named a station of mastery.

The stations of mastery share the eight forms of detachment's own imagery but add a distinct new element the treatise flags explicitly: not just breaking attachment, but mastering the contemplating mind itself, "like a rider on horseback striking at a bandit" who must control the horse as well as defeat the enemy. The deer-not-yet-tamed simile for why beginners are restricted to "a small object" is a rare moment of practical pedagogical caution in a text that otherwise moves through extraordinarily intense visualizations without much comment on pacing or risk.

quiz.q: In the second way detachment leads to the path, what is the person complete in, and what need he not have?
options: the undefiled arises within the detachments, called complete eight liberations; the five later gates are not required
quiz.why: True undefilement arises within the eight detachments, called complete eight liberations, without necessarily the five later gates. In the third way one awakens at the first detachment.

quiz.q: Answering how one can have the eight liberations without the nine concentrations, which is NOT one of the four propositions?
options: both liberation and nirvāṇa, not detachment
quiz.why: The four are: sequential concentrations without liberation; liberation without them; both; and neither, yet the eight detachments. Option A is not among them.

quiz.q: How are the first four stations of mastery distinguished?
options: form within seeing little or much outside; no form within seeing little or much
quiz.why: The first four vary by form within or not and little or much form without; the last four are blue, yellow, red, and white.

quiz.q: What simile illustrates the second sense of "station of mastery"?
options: a rider who not only breaks the enemy line but also masters his horse
quiz.why: Skillfully regulating the contemplating mind is like a rider striking a bandit who not only breaks the enemy line but also masters his own horse; this differs from detachment.

quiz.q: When are the stations of mastery renamed the "eight bases of transcendence"?
options: when through them afflictions are fully severed and the illusory aggregates and bases cease
quiz.why: When afflictions are entirely severed through the stations of mastery and the illusory aggregates and bases cease, they are renamed the eight bases of transcendence.

quiz.q: Where are the stations placed, and why none in the third dhyāna or the formless realm?
options: first two in the first, next two in the second, last four in the fourth; the third has too much happiness and a dull mind; the formless has no form
quiz.why: The first two are in the first dhyāna, the next two in the second, the last four in the fourth; none in the third, where happiness is abundant and the mind dull; none in the formless, which lacks form.

quiz.q: Why contemplate only a little form without, and what simile is used?
options: the path is not yet strong, and much would be hard to master, like an untamed deer not to be let roam far
quiz.why: Because the contemplative path has not yet grown, one takes a small object, fearing a large one hard to master, like an untamed deer not to be let roam far.

quiz.q: Distinguishing good and ill by what they arouse, which is which?
options: what arouses lust is pure form, good; what arouses anger is impure form, ill
quiz.why: Form that arouses lust is pure and called good; form that arouses anger is impure and called ill. Another reading uses wholesome and unwholesome karmic results.

options: the mature mind neither craves the good nor hates the ill, seeing form as conditioned and insubstantial like foam
quiz.why: With a mature mind one neither craves good form nor hates ill form, seeing form as arising from the elements like insubstantial foam, wisdom penetrating the provisional and the real.
